clue.text: Tease oriental combine by haggling

parts.note: to chaff someone is to tease them with banter
E for east, the Orient
a ring is a group combining to fix prices or bids

explanation.surface: Someone teases an Eastern business cartel during a round of bargaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaffering is an old word for bargaining over a price, the same activity as haggling.

clue.text: Jack Hawker is of little worth

explanation.surface: A street seller called Jack is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; the first part means the word that combines with 'Jack' to give a travelling seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap-jack is an old term for a pedlar of low-priced goods, so the word with 'Jack' makes a hawker; and it means inexpensive or of low value.

clue.text: In the services they are responsive to singing.

definitions.text: In the services they are responsive to singing

parts.words: In the services they are responsive to singing
parts.note: 'services' reads as the armed forces but means church services, where sung verses answer one another

explanation.surface: Soldiers and sailors enjoy a good sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' suggests the armed forces; here they are church services, where choirs sing verses in response.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphons are short sentences sung responsively by two halves of a choir in a liturgy.

clue.text: Amorous intrigues at the Quai d'Orsay ?

definitions.text: Amorous intrigues at the Quai d'Orsay ?

parts.words: Amorous intrigues at the Quai d'Orsay ?
parts.note: romantic liaisons are affairs, and the Paris address is that of the French ministry handling dealings with other countries

explanation.surface: Romantic scandals at the French ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Quai d'Orsay is the Paris street that houses the French foreign ministry, so its business is international relations; love affairs there are affairs abroad to an English solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A government's dealings with other nations form its overseas policy, and a love affair in France is one abroad.

clue.text: Makes another subscription and leaves office

explanation.surface: An official renews membership and then quits his post.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-signs it means puts one's name down again; it also means quits a post.

clue.text: Village idiot at Deal is twenty-one

explanation.surface: A simpleton at the Kentish town of Deal turns twenty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, but here 'deal' is the deal of cards: in pontoon (blackjack) an ace and a ten dealt together make twenty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'natural' was an old term for a simple-minded person, and in pontoon a dealt hand worth twenty-one is so called.

clue.text: Grass on the market-place

explanation.surface: Lawn laid out on the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass on' reads as turf lying on a square, but here it is the British slang verb for betraying someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police; a shop is also a place of trade.

clue.text: Anthony's aspirations

explanation.surface: A man named Anthony has ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Hope was an English novelist, author of 'The Prisoner of Zenda'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope wrote 'The Prisoner of Zenda', so the possessive is Hope's; hopes are also wishes or ambitions.

clue.text: Little French number takes the biscuit

parts.note: petit is French for little or small
four is a number

explanation.surface: A small French figure is the most outrageous thing yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous; here 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a small fancy cake or biscuit served with coffee.

clue.text: Officers who show mercy to the school staff ?

parts.note: to give quarter is to spare an enemy, showing mercy
masters are teachers on a school's staff

explanation.surface: A question about army officers who are kind to teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartermasters are military officers in charge of supplies and quarters.

clue.text: Drags out old offences

parts.note: ex- means former, so old
torts are civil wrongs in law

explanation.surface: Someone digs up past misdeeds again.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to drag money or a confession out of someone by force.

clue.text: The sonnet as Milton's instrument (Wordsworth)

parts.note: Wordsworth's sonnet 'Scorn not the Sonnet' says that in Milton's hand the thing became a brass instrument, and the clue asks which

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question about what Wordsworth called the sonnet in Milton's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a quotation question: Wordsworth wrote of Milton that 'in his hand / The Thing became a trumpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the sonnet becomes a brass instrument summoning souls, a loud call to arms in Milton's use.

clue.text: Slips in little German entertainer

parts.note: to pop in is to slip in briefly
Ger is the short form of German

explanation.surface: A small German man sneaks into a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist of chart music is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Take a seat again after ploughing

explanation.surface: Someone sits back down once the field has been ploughed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughing' looks agricultural, but in old British university slang to be ploughed is to fail an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-sit it means to sit once more; in British student slang to plough is to fail an exam, after which one must sit it again.

clue.text: Gardener whose capability is shown at Kew

definitions.text: Gardener whose capability is shown at Kew

parts.words: Gardener whose capability is shown at Kew
parts.note: the eighteenth-century landscape designer nicknamed 'Capability' worked on the royal grounds at Kew

explanation.surface: A horticulturist's skill is on display at the famous botanic gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capability' looks like an ordinary noun but is the nickname of Lancelot Brown, the English landscape gardener; Kew Gardens is the royal botanic garden in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was the great English landscape gardener of the 1700s.

clue.text: Bent over, carefully perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone stoops, cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carefully' is read as 'full of care', and a person laden with care is said to be bowed down with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooped describes something bent over; someone bowed down with care is weighed by worry, read cryptically as 'carefully'.

clue.text: Italian battle colour

explanation.surface: A flag's shade recalls a fight in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Solferino in Lombardy was the scene of an 1859 battle, and the purplish-red dye discovered that year was named after it.

clue.text: Is in better circumstances to make off-hand inventions

indicators.note: the short word is placed inside the longer one here

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

explanation.surface: Someone who is better off is free to invent things on the spur of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumstances' only completes the surface 'in better circumstances'; 'in' puts IS inside IMPROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to create or perform something spontaneously, without preparation.

clue.text: With longing for Mayfair street in complete form

parts.note: Mayfair lies in London's W1 postal district, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
fully means completely, in full form

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for a whole, finished West End street.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London whose postcode is W1.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something wistfully is doing it yearningly, full of longing.

clue.text: Battle-poem at the French Christmas show

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a panto, pantomime, is a traditional British Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: A war poem recited at a French festive entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British family theatre show staged at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto was a naval battle of 1571 and the title of G. K. Chesterton's poem about it.

clue.text: Changes colour through fall

parts.note: 'fall' is the American word for autumn, when leaves turn golden

explanation.surface: Leaves turn as autumn arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves go golden in autumn, turning from green to the shade of a lemon.

clue.text: Doctor's by way of being a listless chap

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; the 's stands for 'is'
per means by means of, by way of

explanation.surface: A doctor seems to be a lethargic man.
explanation.definitionFit: A moper mopes about, a dejected and listless person.

clue.text: She was unwell on the way back

indicators.note: travelling backwards means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: ailed means was ill or unwell

explanation.surface: A woman fell ill on her journey home.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for any woman, so 'She' is defined by an example.

clue.text: United City Guides, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: leads means guides or conducts

explanation.surface: City Guides, the organisation, united.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds United is a well-known English football club, so 'United City' is the city that names it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is the Yorkshire city whose football club is Leeds United.

clue.text: Quickly finish — car's beauty treatment ?

explanation.surface: A rushed end to a car's valeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a car's beauty treatment is the polish of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off is to dispatch a task or meal fast; a car's beauty treatment is a polish, with 'off' read as 'of' plus a further f.

clue.text: Let's —— till six, and then have dinner " (Carroll)

definitions.text: Let's —— till six, and then have dinner

parts.words: Let's —— till six, and then have dinner
parts.note: Tweedledum's words to Tweedledee in 'Through the Looking-Glass', with the missing verb meaning to do battle

explanation.surface: A quotation from Lewis Carroll with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweedledum proposes a battle to Tweedledee in Carroll's 'Through the Looking-Glass'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the verb for a battle or brawl that Tweedledum proposes.

clue.text: Vicar, coming back in our vague direction, may go too far

indicators.note: one group of letters is placed inside the other here
vague suggests something unformed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction

indicators.note: a word coming back is read from right to left

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman returning our way in a muddled direction risks straying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns REV into VER; 'vague' rearranges OUR into ORU, N follows, and 'in' puts VER inside ORUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to run beyond a limit or go on longer than allowed.

clue.text: Time of opportunity locally

parts.note: a chance or gap is one sense, and at 'the local', the British pub, it is the hour the doors unlock

explanation.surface: A chance comes up in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' points to 'the local', British slang for one's regular pub, whose doors unlock at a set time each day.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a chance or opportunity, and pub opening time is when drinking may begin.

clue.text: Turned up showing disdain for informer

explanation.surface: A spy arrived looking scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: A turned-up nose shows disdain, and a nose is also slang for a police informer.

clue.text: German is in agreement, sticking to principles

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other here

parts.note: consent is agreement
ist is the German word for 'is'

explanation.surface: A German is in accord, staying true to his principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps the same stance throughout is unchanging, true to their beliefs.
